description:
draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.9.2 (line 1925 onward) and §10.7.2 (line 3303 onward) define:

- sendSchedulingMessages: Boolean argument on CalendarEvent/set controlling whether the server sends iTIP REQUEST/CANCEL/REPLY messages on event mutation
- noSupportedScheduleMethods SetError: when sendSchedulingMessages is true and at least one recipient has no calendarAddress URI the server can send to, the change MUST be rejected with this SetError

src/event.rs:80-325 (handle_calendar_event_set): sendSchedulingMessages is never read from args. noSupportedScheduleMethods is never produced. grep -n 'sendSchedulingMessages\|noSupportedScheduleMethods' src returns nothing.

PLAN.md §3 describes recurrenceOverrides patch semantics but does not call out sendSchedulingMessages explicitly. It is part of the §5.9 set semantics that PLAN.md row 'CalendarEvent | set | §5.9 | standard set + sendSchedulingMessages' (line 91) flagged for implementation.

Acceptable simplification: the handler can reasonably pass sendSchedulingMessages through to the backend as part of an optional arg struct, since iTIP delivery is fundamentally a backend concern (requires SMTP, address book, etc.). But the SetError mapping is handler-level — when a backend returns 'no schedule method available for recipient X', the handler must produce noSupportedScheduleMethods, not serverFail.

Wire impact: clients that set sendSchedulingMessages:false to suppress invitations on bulk imports will have invitations sent anyway (because the backend never sees the flag and falls back to its default). For the inverse case — client sets true and backend can't deliver — the client gets serverFail instead of noSupportedScheduleMethods, losing the ability to react meaningfully.

Fix: add sendSchedulingMessages to a CalendarEventSetArgs struct or pass directly to backend create/update/destroy as part of a context. Add a noSupportedScheduleMethods variant to BackendSetError or extend SetErrorType so backends can signal it.

Test gap: no test.
title: CalendarEvent/set sendSchedulingMessages arg unimplemented; noSupportedScheduleMethods SetError never produced
